sentences.text: Petitioner is the proprietor of a concern called Welcome Traders, which is engaged in the business of stock and sale of rice, grocery items and cattle feed.
According to the petitioner, petitioner is functioning with all necessary statutory licenses, required for conducting his business, evident from Exts. P1 to P3.

On 14.02.2017, third respondent and party conducted a search in the shop room of the petitioner and seized 2960 kilograms of raw rice and 4600 kilograms of boiled rice, as per Ext.
P4 Mahazar.

In Ext. P4, it is stated that the seizure was effected by the third respondent under the reasonable belief that the seized rice is ration rice meant for distribution through public distribution system.
According to the petitioner, the third respondent did not mention anything in Ext. P4 to show that the seized rice is ration rice.
Other contentions are also W.P.(C).
NO. 7084 OF 2017 raised and ultimately seeks the relief of releasing the product seized from the petitioner.
During the pendency of the writ petition certain developments have taken place from the side of the respondents.

The second respondent has issued a show cause notice to the petitioner asking to show cause, why the seized rice shall not be sold in open market and thereafter, Ext. P6 order is passed dated 04.03.2017 by which, it was decided to sell of the rice in open market.
These documents are produced by the petitioner along with I.A. No. 4516/2017.

2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Government Pleader and perused the documents on record and the pleadings put forth by the petitioner.
3.

This Court had occasion to consider a similar situation and had rendered a judgment in W.P.(C).
No. 33107/2014, dated 06.03.2015, in which the respondents were permitted to sell off the kerosene seized with a rider that if it is ultimately found that the product is not ration article, the respondents will be liable to pay the open W.P.(C). NO. 7084 OF 2017 market value of the goods as on the date of seizure.
I think the same methodology can be adopted in this writ petition also.

4. Therefore, there will be a direction to the second respondent to pay the market value of the product as on the date of seizure, if ultimately, it is found that the products seized are not ration articles and the petitioner has procured the same from the open market.
Every endeavour shall be made to attain finality to the adjudication proceedings, at the earliest.
Writ petition is disposed of accordingly.

SHAJI P. CHALY JUDGE DCS John Peter Ampurose vs State Of Kerala on 13 December, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21936886/
